d: the qualities and facts that make a person or group distinct from others
ex: Language and culture are important parts of a person's identity.

d: a strong effect or influence that something has on a situation
ex: The new road had a major impact on the local economy.

d: a possible effect or result that follows from an action or decision
ex: The court's decision has serious implications for all online companies.

d: something that encourages a person to act or work harder
ex: The company offers a bonus as an incentive for staff to meet their targets.

d: a number or list used to measure or compare changes over time
ex: The price index rose by two percent in the last quarter.

d: a sign or measure that shows what is happening in a situation
ex: Unemployment is an important indicator of how healthy an economy is.

d: a difference in wealth, rights or opportunities between people or groups
ex: Income inequality has grown in many cities over the past twenty years.

d: a general rise in prices, which reduces how much money can buy
ex: High inflation makes it harder for families to save money each month.

d: the power to change how other people think or behave
ex: Parents have a strong influence on the choices their children make.

d: the basic systems of a country, such as roads, power and water supply
ex: The government plans to invest in roads, bridges and other infrastructure.

d: a new plan or action taken to solve a problem or improve something
ex: The city launched an initiative to plant ten thousand trees this year.

d: damage done to a person's body, often in an accident or a fall
ex: The footballer returned to training after a serious knee injury.

d: a new idea, method or product that changes the way things are done
ex: Innovation in medicine has helped doctors treat diseases that were once deadly.

d: a clear and deep understanding of a complex subject or situation
ex: The interview gave the researcher valuable insight into family life.

d: a careful official examination of something to check its condition or safety
ex: The health inspector visited the restaurant for a routine inspection.

d: a particular example or case of something happening
ex: In one instance, the company paid its workers late for several months.

d: an organisation such as a bank, school or hospital that serves the public
ex: The bank is one of the oldest financial institutions in the country.

d: an agreement that pays money if you suffer loss, damage or illness
ex: Travellers should buy health insurance before they leave the country.

d: the quality of being honest and having strong moral principles
ex: Judges are expected to act with complete integrity at all times.

d: a plan or purpose to do something in the future
ex: She has no intention of leaving the company before next year.

d: the act of becoming involved in something that is not your business
ex: The manager was criticised for interference in the work of his team.

d: an explanation of what something means, or of how it should be performed
ex: Different readers may have different interpretations of the same poem.

d: a careful and official search for facts about a crime or problem
ex: The police opened an investigation into the theft at the bank.

d: a person or organisation that puts money into a business, project or property
ex: Foreign investors showed interest in the new technology company.

d: one of the foods or materials that are mixed together to make something
ex: Fresh tomatoes are the main ingredient in this simple sauce.

d: a person or animal that lives in a particular place
ex: The island has about five hundred inhabitants, most of them fishermen.

d: a natural ability or urge to behave in a certain way without thinking
ex: Animals have a strong instinct to protect their young from danger.

d: the ability to learn, understand and think clearly, or information gathered by agencies
ex: The company is investing heavily in artificial intelligence for its products.

d: a period of time between two events, or a space between two things
ex: Buses leave the station at regular intervals throughout the day.

d: a complete list of goods or items that a business has in stock
ex: The store checks its inventory every month to avoid running out of stock.

d: a sign or piece of information that suggests something is true
ex: There is little indication that the problem will be solved soon.

d: a false idea or image that seems to be real but is not
ex: The mirrors in the room create an illusion that it is much bigger.

d: a lack of knowledge or awareness about a subject or situation
ex: Many people act out of ignorance rather than from a wish to harm others.

d: an event, especially one that is unpleasant, unusual or involves danger
ex: Police are investigating an incident at the station late last night.

d: to recognise someone or something and say what they are
ex: Doctors can identify the illness after a simple blood test.

d: to explain something clearly with examples, or to draw pictures for a book
ex: The teacher used simple examples to illustrate the rule of grammar.

d: to force a rule, tax or duty on people, usually by official authority
ex: The government decided to impose a new tax on imported cars.

d: to include something as a part of a larger whole
ex: The designers incorporated solar panels into the roof of the building.

d: to show that something is true or likely, or to point to something
ex: The results indicate that most students enjoy learning online.

d: to reach a conclusion from evidence or information rather than being told directly
ex: From her silence, I could infer that she did not agree.

d: to begin or start something, such as a process or an investigation
ex: The council will initiate a review of the city's parking rules.

d: to say firmly that something must happen or that something is true
ex: The doctor insisted that the patient rest for at least a week.

d: to examine something carefully, often to check its quality or safety
ex: Officers inspect the factory every year to check safety standards.

d: to combine two things so that they work together as one whole
ex: The school wants to integrate technology into every subject in the curriculum.

d: to explain or decide the meaning of something, such as a law
ex: Judges must interpret the law carefully before making a decision.

d: to become involved in a situation in order to change or stop it
ex: The judge decided to intervene when the two lawyers began to shout.

d: to carefully examine the facts about a crime, accident or problem
ex: The committee will investigate how the money was spent last year.

d: to separate a person, animal or thing from others so that it is alone
ex: Doctors isolate patients with infections to stop the disease from spreading.

d: to put money into a business, project or property to make a profit
ex: Many families invest part of their savings in government bonds.

d: to put a plan, rule or system into action so that it takes effect
ex: The new government plans to implement the reforms within six months.

d: to suggest that something is true without saying it directly
ex: Her smile seemed to imply that she already knew the answer.

d: to receive money, property or a title from someone who has died
ex: She inherited the family house and a small piece of land.

d: to stop someone while they are speaking or doing something
ex: Please do not interrupt the speaker until the presentation is finished.

d: exactly the same as something else in every detail
ex: The two twins wore identical blue jackets to the wedding.

d: treating everyone equally and not favouring any side
ex: A good judge must be impartial and listen to both sides fairly.

d: suggested or understood without being directly stated
ex: There was an implicit agreement that nobody would mention the mistake.

d: certain to happen and impossible to avoid or prevent
ex: After the long drought, a rise in food prices seemed inevitable.

d: relaxed and casual, not following official rules or formal style
ex: The meeting was informal, so everyone sat in a circle on the floor.

d: happening at the start, or the first in a series of stages
ex: The initial results of the study were positive, but more tests are needed.

d: introducing new ideas, methods or products that are different and creative
ex: The start-up developed an innovative device that cleans water quickly.

d: very strong, extreme, or full of great effort or emotion
ex: The athletes trained with intense focus for many months before the race.

d: impossible to see, or hidden from view
ex: Air is invisible, but we can feel the wind moving around us.

d: not connected with the subject or not important to the matter
ex: The judge said that the old evidence was irrelevant to the new case.

d: far away from other places, people or things
ex: The village is isolated in the mountains and only reached by a single road.

d: protected from a disease, or unaffected by something harmful
ex: Children who have had the disease are usually immune to it for life.

d: not enough, or not good enough for a particular purpose
ex: The school's library is inadequate for the needs of four hundred students.

d: not going straight to the point, or caused by something else first
ex: The new law had an indirect effect on small farms in the region.

d: having a strong effect on how other people think or act
ex: She is one of the most influential writers in the field of law.

d: used to emphasise a statement or to agree with something strongly
ex: The results were indeed surprising, and many experts changed their opinion.

d: to a greater degree than before, or more and more over time
ex: Students are increasingly using tablets instead of paper notebooks.

d: at the beginning, before any later changes or developments
ex: Initially, the project was expected to take only three months.

d: in a way that cannot be avoided or prevented from happening
ex: Inevitably, some students found the exam harder than they expected.

d: in the best or most perfect way, if conditions were just right
ex: Ideally, every child should have access to a good library.

d: without the help or control of others; on your own
ex: The students completed the research project independently, without any help.

d: on purpose, not by accident or by mistake
ex: The manager intentionally delayed the report to avoid the meeting.
